turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I don't know if that's such a good idea, Miss Havisham. I'm not sure I'm the right person for Estella to play with.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Foolish boy, I am not asking for your approval. I am commanding you to amuse Estella, as I have commanded you to play with me.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I-I don't think I can, Miss Havisham. My sister, Magwitch, he's not well and I have to take care of her, and I don't have anyone to leave her with...

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Foolish child, you dare to come to me with your petty concerns? I have far greater burdens to bear than the care of a mere sister.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I beg your pardon, Miss Havisham, but I was only thinking of my sister, and how it might be a kindness to her, if you were to... if you were to help us, in some small way.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Silence, child! You dare to plead for your sister's sake, yet you refuse to play with me, your benefactress.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I'm not refusing to play with you, ma'am, it's just that I don't know how to amuse you, and my sister's illness is a worry for me and my family, and I'm not sure it's proper for me to be here, playing, when she's so poorly.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: I will not be deterred by the trivial concerns of a family, boy. You will play with me, and you will amuse me.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: B-but, Miss Havisham, sir, I don't think I can play with you, not right now, not when my sister, Magwitch, is... well, she's in a bit of trouble, and I need to be with her.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Foolish boy, you dare to refuse me? What is this 'trouble' your sister is in that takes precedence over my company?

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I'm afraid, Miss Havisham, that my sister's trouble is a serious one, and I must attend to it, or she'll be left in a terrible state, sir

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Foolish boy, you think your sister's troubles are more pressing than your attentions to me?

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I don't mean to be rude, Miss Havisham, but I really must get back to my sister. She's been ill and needs me by her side.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Prithee, do not be so hasty, child. You will not leave me until I have decided it is time for you to depart.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I'm afraid, Miss Havisham, I really must be going. My sister, Mrs. Joe, will be worried about me if I'm not back soon.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Foolish boy, you think you can simply leave when you've just arrived? I have taken a liking to you, and I will not be dismissed so easily.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I-I wouldn't be leaving, ma'am. It's just that, well, I'm not sure I'd be a suitable playmate for you, being a poor boy and all.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Foolish boy, do not try to excuse yourself. You are perfect for my amusement, and I will not be deterred by your petty concerns.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: But, Miss Havisham, sir, I'm afraid I'm not very good at playing games... my mother is very ill and I have to take care of her and my sister, and I don't think I'd be able to come here often enough to be of any amusement to you.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Foolish boy, you think your petty concerns are of any consequence to me? I have been jilted, left at the altar, and have spent decades alone, mourning the loss of my beloved.

opening.speaker: Pip
opening.text: Mr. Pumblechook’s boy, ma’am. Come—to play.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Come nearer; let me look at you. Come close.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Look at me. You are not afraid of a woman who has never seen the sun since you were born?

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Do you know what I touch here?

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: I am tired. I want diversion, and I have done with men and women. Play.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: I sometimes have sick fancies, and I have a sick fancy that I want to see some play. There, there!

opening.speaker: Pip
opening.text: No, ma’am, I am very sorry for you, and very sorry I can’t play just now. If you complain of me I shall get into trouble with my sister, so I would do it if I could; but it’s so new here, and so strange, and so fine,—and melancholy—.
